A1.justification: Both complete 38-page PDFs describe FlowInOne and include readable main text and Appendices A-G. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that changes are confined to pages 1 and 11.

before.justification: v2 reports original VP-Bench experiments, automated and human evaluations, architectural ablations, robustness tests, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including benchmark comparisons, human evaluations, and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix G retain the same visual encoding, latent flow matching, Dual-Path Spatially-Adaptive Modulation, training losses, and inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VisPrompt-5M training data and eight-category VP-Bench coverage. The appendix perturbation and resolution test scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain OmniGen2, FLUX.1-Kontext-dev, Qwen-Image-Edit-2509, and Nano Banana as comparators. Comparator configurations in the ablation studies are unchanged.

E3.justification: Training settings, benchmark splits, baseline procedures, evaluation metrics, VLM judges, and human evaluation sampling remain identical in Section 5 and Appendices B, F, and G.

E4.justification: The architectural and training-strategy ablations in Table 4, error and robustness analyses in Appendix A, qualitative examples in Appendix C, and hyperparameter analyses in Table 12 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 and Table 5 retain the same Fleiss' kappa and Kendall's W agreement statistics. There are no changes to run-count, seed, uncertainty, or significance reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative output examples are unchanged, including the appendices. The revision changes how performance is summarized, rather than the reported experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Equations 1-19, metric definitions, and appendix layout algorithm and complexity reasoning remain identical. No theoretical assumptions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the performance claim from surpassing both open-source and commercial systems to leading open-source models while remaining competitive with commercial systems. The proposed framework, dataset, and benchmark contributions are retained.

C2.justification: The conclusion qualifies its interpretation of commercial comparisons as competitiveness, aligning it with the existing Section 5.2 discussion. Mechanistic explanations, failure analyses, and Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training costs, data-processing instructions, evaluation prompts, and resource-access information are unchanged in Section 5.1 and the appendices.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the claimed novelty of the vision-centric flow-matching formulation are unchanged. No cited work or methodological relationship to prior research is added or revised.

P1.justification: A few sentences in the abstract and conclusion are rewritten, including the performance qualification and the description of a 'promising foundation.' The arXiv version/date stamp changes; section and appendix organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Visible changes are limited to local line wrapping in the edited paragraphs and repositioning of the updated arXiv margin stamp. All figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revised commercial-performance claim better matches the unchanged evidence: Table 1 places Nano Banana above FlowInOne under three of four evaluators, including human overall pass rates of 45.9% versus 44.9%. This improves consistency between the summaries and Section 5.2. The improvement is limited: the retained claim of open-source leadership across all tasks remains overbroad, since human text-to-image scores are 64.5% for FlowInOne versus 71.0% for OmniGen2.
